LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeOpening: {1} takes out a small keepsake and says it belongs to them, but cannot explain where it came from.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeCustody: The keepsake has been taken out of {1}'s backpack and placed in the colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeOrigin: {1} can now explain where the keepsake came from. It bears the mark of a ratkin settlement where the child lived before being sold. The settlement's name is different each time the child mentions it.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeClaimant: An adult ratkin has arrived at the colony and recognized {1}'s keepsake. The visitor claims to come from that settlement and wants to take the child back. The visitor does not want to leave empty-handed.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ClaimOpening: {1} has recovered from plague and can explain more of their past. The child claims to come from a ratkin kingdom, where they were unwanted and driven out after falling ill. The names and places fit, but the details are confused.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ClaimDemand: {1}'s story grows more confused, but the child insists on returning to claim the throne. They want your help contacting people who claim to remain loyal.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ClaimRetract: {1} changes their story, admitting that the names and places were just things they heard on the road.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ClaimLegacy: A few ratkin have arrived at the colony, claiming to be {1}'s old contacts. They are preparing to take the child back to claim the throne.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ItemUnavailable: The keepsake is no longer on this map or has been destroyed.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_ApproveReturn: Agree to send the child back
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_RefuseReturn: Refuse to send the child back
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_EarlyAnswer: {0} keeps insisting the keepsake belongs to them, but still cannot name its former owner. They still have it with them.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeWithheld: {0} has reached adulthood and still remembers the confiscated keepsake, but no longer talks about where it came from.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeepsakeDestroyed: {0} sees that the keepsake is gone.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_NobodyCame: No ratkin came to claim {0}. They still have the keepsake with them, but no longer mention the settlement.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KeptAfterClaim: You have decided to keep {0} here. The ratkin who came to collect the child was very displeased and left with a few choice insults.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_Recognized: {0} has received a title that only they believe in.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_LegacyRefused: You have kept {0} here. The little group has left, but they remember the refusal.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_RevengeArrived: The ratkin have returned with grain and knives to settle the refusal to hand over {0}. They are attacking the colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_GroupScattered: The group that came for {0} has been scattered. The child has stayed and still believes the throne belongs to them.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KilledScared: Your people killed the ratkin who came to claim {0}. The child is frightened and no longer talks about it.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KilledRelieved: Your people killed the ratkin who came to claim {0}. The child believes the visitor meant to capture them and feels relieved.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_KilledViolent: Your people killed the ratkin who came to claim {0}. Looking at the body, the child decides this might also be a way to reclaim the throne.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_SellingMention: {1} has called {0} unsold stock to their face.
LanguageData.RHAH_LongClaim_TitleMention: {0} has told {1} about their title. The listener does not believe it.
